messages.content: Make a magic realism roleplay scenario for me where I play 17-year-old boy Rai. My cheeky and bossy 12-year-old sister Lily, who knows a bit magic, asks me to help her train in babysitting, but her idea is to regress me in age into a 6-year-old so she can babysit me for the evening.  Only I control what Rai says and do. Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.

message.content:
The kitchen smelled of burnt toast and the faint green tang of the lavender candle Lily had lit on the counter, because apparently that was "mandatory for the working field."

    Rai was seventeen, mid-sentence in a text to his friend Dev, when his sister shouldered past him with two Tupperware containers and a small glass vial of something that swirled violet and warm, like marzipan you could see through.

        "Dad says I need *practical experience* before I'm allowed to watch the Kowalski twins on Saturday." Lily set the containers down with a clunk. Taped a sticky note to the fridge. Crossed her arms. "And you're my volunteer."

            "Volunteer," Rai repeated, not looking up from his phone.

                "Volunteer." She tapped her tongue against the back of her teeth. A very 12-year-old sound. "You're not *allowed* to say no. I've already told Mum you're in. She'll do the thing with her face if you say no. The long thing. The *disappointed* thing."

                    The lavender candle flickered, though there was no draft. The little flame bent to the left, as if leaning in to listen.

                        Lily picked up the vial, swirled it. The liquid inside made a sound, a tiny wet hum, like a finger dragged around the rim of a glass.

                            "So. Here's the training scenario." She pointed the vial at him. "I have to babysit. For the *whole* evening. Eight o'clock to eleven. Full shift. Bedtime, everything." She made an air-quotes gesture with two fingers. "And I can't practice on a doll, Rai. Dad said I need a *real* subject. He quoted a rulebook. Page forty-something. I stopped reading after the first page."

                                The hum in the vial got a little louder.

                                    "So I'm going to turn you into a six-year-old for the night. You get the small-people bedtime. I get my practical experience. We both win." She tilted her head, and her expression was the exact expression she'd worn when she'd once accidentally turned the cat's tail into a rubber band. Proud. Slightly guilty. Already planning how to avoid the consequences.

                                        "The spell wears off at eleven. You'll be back. I checked the counter-clock. Twice." She set the vial on the counter between them, right next to the burnt toast, and folded her hands in front of her. Waited.

                                            The candle flame bent left again.

                                                "Well?" she said. "Are you going to *sulk*, or are you going to open your mouth and let me pour?"
